channel.title: Geno
channel.description: Notes, releases and design writing from the Geno project.

item.title: Geno 0.5.0: main now speaks in exit codes
item.description: Geno 0.5.0 makes main() -> Int your process exit status, adds named constructor arguments, and runs an Async value at most once. Here is what changed and how to migrate.

item.title: The playground runs the real compiler
item.description: Most language playgrounds send your code to a server. Geno's runs the actual CLI inside your browser tab, with Python compiled to WebAssembly and a 600 KB bundle of the toolchain.

item.title: Examples are the specification
item.description: Ordinary Geno functions must carry at least one example clause, and geno test runs them all. Why we made examples mandatory, and what that buys you when a model writes the code.

item.title: Why Geno writes end func
item.description: Braces and indentation work well for people with editors. Generated code needs boundaries that survive truncation, reformatting and streaming, so every Geno block closes by name.

item.title: Fail closed: how capabilities work
item.description: A Geno program cannot read a file, open a socket or start a process unless the command that runs it says so. Here is how capability gating works on each surface, including where it does not protect you.

item.title: What we measure, and what we don't claim yet
item.description: Geno's compiled Python lands at a median 1.60x the time of hand-written Python across 53 measured problems. Whether models write more correct code in Geno is a question we have not answered publicly, and here is why.

item.title: Geno, written in Geno
item.description: The repository includes a lexer, parser, type checker and interpreter for Geno, written in about 8,400 lines of Geno. What it covers, what it does not, and why we keep it honest with a parity check.
